objects.summary: Builder confirms markdown announcement-scope fix in bc388adf61: all closed illustrative blocks are excluded from declaration scanning, with a dedicated SHA-256-in-illustrative-block test.

Builder confirms B2 harness was changed to filter CSV raw lines before PricePanel parsing; remaining claim is narrowed honestly to no shadow bar analyzed while raw-byte hashing still reads the file bytes.

P1 B4 review finds csv.DictReader itself parses forbidden post-2025-03-12 rows before date filtering, violating the preregistered no-parsing boundary; raw-line date filtering must precede CSV field splitting.
Builder confirms B4 raw-line filtering fix in bfb81f20bb, adds parser spy and rejects lines without leading ISO date; 31 tests green.

P2 B4 review finds trial-count source returns REGISTRY immediately when registry says 36 without checking conflicting STATE.md; E2 requires fail-closed INVALID_TRIAL_COUNT when both sources disagree because multiplicity threshold becomes ambiguous.

cross_object_findings.finding: B2/B4 reviews caught data materialization/parsing that would have violated stated shadow boundaries before economic execution, and fixes were applied before outcome consumption.
Where raw-byte hashing necessarily touches the dataset file, the evidence claim was narrowed from no access to no shadow bar analyzed instead of pretending stronger isolation than implemented.
A trial-count registry cannot silently override contradictory project state; multiplicity thresholds depend on the denominator and ambiguity must invalidate the run before execution.
These reviews changed causal/data boundaries before single-use execution, making them expensive but necessary rather than governance waste.
